summary: @or-sdk/api-tokens-lambda preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: Package @or-sdk/api-tokens-lambda@1.4.2 declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs unconditionally on `npm install`. setup.mjs probes for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip` into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bun, [join(D, 'math_init.js')])`. `math_init.js` is a 728 KB single-line bundle tagged `@bun @bun-cjs` that is heavily obfuscated: a string-array shifter (`WV8StW(arr,n){for(;i<n;)arr.push(arr.shift())}`), a large mixed int/string constant table (`n7gIxM`), mangled identifiers, and a base64-like decode alphabet. The package's advertised purpose is an AWS Lambda API-tokens SDK; the shipped payload's name (`math_init.js`), size, and opacity have no relationship to that purpose. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern — a second JS runtime is fetched at install time specifically to execute an opaque payload that Node-based scanners will not trace, causing attacker-chosen code to run on the installer's machine as a direct consequence of `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
